problems.title: Branch or select
problems.statement: An if/else with sides of 3 and 4 instructions. A branch costs 2 instructions of overhead; predication costs 1 select.

parts.prompt: Branch, divergent warp?
Predicated, any warp?
Branch, uniform warp, averaged over warps that take each side equally often?

problems.solution: (a) $3 + 4 + 2 = 9$. (b) $3 + 4 + 1 = 8$. (c) $(3 + 2 + 4 + 2)/2 = 5.5$. Predication wins only if enough warps would diverge.

problems.title: The break-even point
problems.statement: Both sides cost $k$ instructions; a branch has 3 instructions of overhead; predication runs both sides plus 1 select. A fraction $f$ of warps diverge.

parts.prompt: For k = 5, the f above which predication is cheaper?
For k = 10?
For k = 1, is predication cheaper even at f = 0? (1 = yes, 0 = no)

problems.solution: Predication wins when $k(1 - f) < 2$, i.e. $f > 1 - 2/k$: (a) 0.6, (b) 0.8. (c) For $k = 1$: $1 - 2 = -1 < 0$, so predication wins always ($3$ vs $4$). Short sides: predicate. Long sides: branch unless divergence is very likely.

problems.title: Border checks, 32 × 8 blocks
problems.statement: A 1024 × 1024 image, 32 × 8 blocks, so each warp is one row of 32 pixels. The kernel does if (x == 0 || x == W-1 || y == 0 || y == H-1) border(); else interior();

parts.prompt: Total warps?
Warps that diverge?
Warps that are uniformly on the border?

hints: A warp diverges if it holds both border and interior pixels.
problems.solution: (a) $1024 \times 32 = 32{,}768$. (b) The first and last warp of each interior row (rows 1–1022) hold one border pixel: $2 \times 1022 = 2044$. (c) Rows 0 and 1023: 32 warps each, all border. About 6% of warps diverge.

problems.title: Border checks, 16 × 16 blocks
problems.statement: Same image and kernel, 16 × 16 blocks: each warp covers two half-rows of 16 pixels (rows y and y + 1, 16 consecutive x).

parts.prompt: Warps that diverge?

hints: Warps touching column 0 or column 1023: all of them diverge.
Warps covering rows 0–1 or 1022–1023 away from the side columns: half border, half interior.
problems.solution: Left and right edges: 512 row-pairs × 2 sides = 1,024 warps, all mixed. Top and bottom: the row pair (0, 1) or (1022, 1023) in the 62 interior column groups, mixed too: 124. Total 1148, fewer than the 2044 with 32 × 8, because a warp covers two rows: one warp per row-pair per side instead of one per row. Block shape changes divergence, not just memory access.

problems.title: A rare, expensive side
problems.statement: Each lane needs a 500-instruction fix-up with probability 0.001, else 5 instructions of normal work. A branch costs 2 instructions of overhead.

parts.prompt: Predicated (both sides always, plus 1 select): instructions per warp?
Branching: expected instructions per warp?
Which is faster, and by how much?

problems.solution: (a) $500 + 5 + 1 = 506$. (b) $7 + 0.0315 \times 500 = 22.8$. (c) Branching, 22× faster. Never predicate the expensive rare case.

problems.title: What the compiler will do

parts.prompt: Which is most likely to compile to a select instruction?
In this course's simulator, which construct is counted as a branch?

problems.solution: (a) The ternary with trivial sides. A call to an expensive function, or any loop, stays a branch. (b) if, while and for are branches; ternaries and Math functions are treated as predicated.

problems.title: What clamping reads
problems.statement: A 3 × 3 blur over a 1024 × 1024 image clamps neighbour coordinates to the image (clamp-to-edge).

parts.prompt: Neighbour reads (of the 9 per pixel) whose coordinates had to be clamped, over the whole image?
As a fraction of all reads, in %?

hints: Corner pixels have 5 out-of-image neighbours; other edge pixels 3.
problems.solution: (a) 4 corners × 5 + 4 × 1,022 edge pixels × 3 = 12,284. (b) 0.130%. Clamping costs a couple of min/max instructions on every read, and re-reads a few edge pixels; in exchange no warp diverges.

problems.title: A chain of cases
problems.statement: A lane's case c ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3} is uniform random. Case costs: 3, 5, 8, 12 instructions. Option P: compute all four and select with 3 selects. Option B: if (c==0) … else if (c==1) … else if (c==2) … else …, with 2 instructions per test that any lane reaches.

parts.prompt: Option P, per warp?
Option B, per warp, assuming every warp contains all four cases?
Option B after sorting lanes so each warp has one case: average per warp?

hints: With all cases present, all three tests run.
Sorted: case 0 needs 1 test, case 1 two, cases 2 and 3 three.
problems.solution: (a) $3 + 5 + 8 + 12 + 3 = 31$. (b) All bodies and all 3 tests: $28 + 6 = 34$. (c) $(5 + 9 + 14 + 18)/4 = 11.5$. Random data: predication wins narrowly. Sorted data: branching wins by almost 3×. The right code depends on the data's arrangement, not only the code.

problems.title: Rules of thumb

parts.prompt: Short and data-dependent
Long but warp-uniform (depends only on blockIdx)
Long and data-dependent

problems.solution: (a) Predicate: both sides are cheap. (b) Branch: no warp diverges, so the branch costs two instructions. (c) Restructure so warps agree (sort, bin or compact); otherwise you pay both long sides.

problems.title: Branch-free idioms

parts.prompt: Which compute i clamped to [0, n−1]?

problems.solution: The first two are both clamps (for $n \ge 1$ the order doesn't matter), and the nested ternary is a predicated clamp. Math.min(i, n-1) alone doesn't handle negatives.
